quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Matching Word Forms in a List
quests.faultySentence: The new apartment is spacious, modern, and has good lighting.
quests.correctedSentence: The new apartment is spacious, modern, and well-lit.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'spacious' and 'modern' are adjectives, the third item should match that form: 'well-lit', not the verb phrase 'has good lighting'.
quests.nativeTip: The first two items are adjectives — should the third item also be an adjective?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Matching Word Forms in a List
quests.faultySentence: Her job requires creativity, patience, and to communicate well.
quests.correctedSentence: Her job requires creativity, patience, and communication.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'creativity' and 'patience' are nouns, the third item should also be a noun: 'communication', not the infinitive phrase 'to communicate well'.
quests.nativeTip: The first two items are nouns — should the third item also be a noun?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Matching Word Forms in a List
quests.faultySentence: The hikers packed water, energy bars, and bringing a first-aid kit.
quests.correctedSentence: The hikers packed water, energy bars, and a first-aid kit.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'water' and 'energy bars' are nouns, the third item should match: 'a first-aid kit', not the verb phrase 'bringing a first-aid kit'.
quests.nativeTip: The first two items in the list are simple nouns — should the third item also be a noun?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Matching Verb Forms in a Series
quests.faultySentence: Every morning, she wakes up, showers, and getting dressed for work.
quests.correctedSentence: Every morning, she wakes up, showers, and gets dressed for work.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'wakes' and 'showers' are simple present tense, the last verb should match: 'gets dressed', not the -ing form 'getting dressed'.
quests.nativeTip: The other verbs in the list are simple present tense — should the last one match?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Matching Verb Forms in a Series
quests.faultySentence: The technician diagnosed the problem, ordered the part, and installing it the next day.
quests.correctedSentence: The technician diagnosed the problem, ordered the part, and installed it the next day.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'diagnosed' and 'ordered' are simple past tense, the last verb should match: 'installed', not the -ing form 'installing'.
quests.nativeTip: The other verbs are in simple past tense — should the last one match?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Matching Verb Forms After To
quests.faultySentence: The company plans to hire more staff, expand its offices, and increasing marketing spending next year.
quests.correctedSentence: The company plans to hire more staff, expand its offices, and increase marketing spending next year.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'hire' and 'expand' are base-form verbs following 'plans to', the last verb should also be base form: 'increase', not 'increasing'.
quests.nativeTip: The other verbs after 'plans to' are in base form — should the last one match?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Not Only...But Also
quests.faultySentence: She is not only talented but also she works hard.
quests.correctedSentence: She is not only talented but also hardworking.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'not only' is followed by the adjective 'talented', 'but also' should also be followed by an adjective: 'hardworking', not a full clause.
quests.nativeTip: 'Not only' is followed by an adjective, 'talented' — should 'but also' be followed by the same kind of word?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Either...Or
quests.faultySentence: You can either call the office or you can send an email.
quests.incorrectPart: or you can send an email
quests.correctedSentence: You can either call the office or send an email.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'either' is followed by the base verb 'call', 'or' should also be followed by a base verb: 'send', not a repeated subject and modal.
quests.nativeTip: 'Either' is followed by the base verb 'call' — should 'or' be followed by the same kind of word?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Both...And
quests.faultySentence: The proposal was both cost-effective and it saved time.
quests.correctedSentence: The proposal was both cost-effective and time-saving.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'both' is followed by the adjective 'cost-effective', 'and' should also be followed by an adjective: 'time-saving', not a full clause.
quests.nativeTip: 'Both' is followed by the adjective 'cost-effective' — should 'and' be followed by the same kind of word?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Matching Gerunds in a List
quests.faultySentence: Her hobbies include painting, hiking, and to read novels.
quests.correctedSentence: Her hobbies include painting, hiking, and reading novels.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'painting' and 'hiking' are gerunds, the last item should also be a gerund: 'reading', not the infinitive 'to read'.
quests.nativeTip: The other hobbies are in the -ing form — should the last one match?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Matching Infinitives in a List
quests.faultySentence: He wants to travel more, to save money, and spending less time at work.
quests.correctedSentence: He wants to travel more, to save money, and to spend less time at work.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'to travel' and 'to save' are infinitives, the last item should also be an infinitive: 'to spend', not the gerund 'spending'.
quests.nativeTip: The other goals after 'wants' use the infinitive form 'to' plus a verb — should the last one match?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Matching Gerunds in a List
quests.faultySentence: The training covers writing reports, managing time, and how to lead meetings.
quests.correctedSentence: The training covers writing reports, managing time, and leading meetings.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'writing' and 'managing' are gerunds, the last item should also be a gerund: 'leading', not the phrase 'how to lead'.
quests.nativeTip: The other skills covered are in the -ing form — should the last one match?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Comparing Equivalent Items
quests.faultySentence: My commute is longer than my coworker.
quests.correctedSentence: My commute is longer than my coworker's.
quests.ruleExplanation: To compare like with like, the sentence should compare commutes, not a commute to a person: 'than my coworker's [commute]'.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence compares a commute to a person — should it compare the commute to the coworker's commute instead?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Comparing Equivalent Items
quests.faultySentence: The population of this city is larger than that city.
quests.correctedSentence: The population of this city is larger than that city's.
quests.ruleExplanation: To compare populations with populations, not a population to a city, the sentence needs 'than that city's [population]'.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence compares a population to a whole city — should it compare the population to that city's population instead?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Comparing Equivalent Items
quests.faultySentence: The quality of the new printer is better than the old printer.
quests.correctedSentence: The quality of the new printer is better than the old printer's.
quests.ruleExplanation: To compare quality with quality rather than quality with an object, the sentence needs 'than the old printer's [quality]'.
quests.nativeTip: This sentence compares quality to a printer — should it compare quality to the old printer's quality instead?

quests.conceptTitle: Comparison: As...As for Equal Comparisons
quests.faultySentence: This laptop is as fast than the previous model.
quests.correctedSentence: This laptop is as fast as the previous model.
quests.ruleExplanation: Equal comparisons use 'as...as' throughout, so the sentence needs 'as fast as', not 'as fast than'.
quests.nativeTip: Equal comparisons use 'as...as', not a mix of 'as' and another word — what's the correct second word?

quests.conceptTitle: Comparison: As...As for Equal Comparisons
quests.faultySentence: The new policy isn't as strict than the old one.
quests.correctedSentence: The new policy isn't as strict as the old one.
quests.ruleExplanation: The structure 'as...as' is used even in negative comparisons, so the sentence needs 'as strict as', not 'as strict than'.
quests.nativeTip: Even in a negative sentence, equal comparisons use 'as...as' — what's the correct second word here?

quests.conceptTitle: Comparison: As...As for Equal Comparisons
quests.faultySentence: Her presentation was as informative than the keynote speech.
quests.correctedSentence: Her presentation was as informative as the keynote speech.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since this is an equal comparison, the sentence needs 'as informative as' throughout, not a mix with 'than'.
quests.nativeTip: Equal comparisons keep the same word on both sides of the adjective — what should replace 'than' here?

quests.conceptTitle: Comparison: Completing the Than Clause
quests.faultySentence: She earns more money than working at her old job.
quests.incorrectPart: than working at her old job
quests.correctedSentence: She earns more money than she did at her old job.
quests.correctedPart: than she did at her old job
quests.ruleExplanation: The 'than' clause should be a complete comparison with a subject and verb, so the sentence needs 'than she did at her old job'.
quests.nativeTip: The comparison needs a complete clause with a subject and verb — what's missing here?

quests.conceptTitle: Comparison: Subject-Verb Agreement in Than Clauses
quests.faultySentence: This restaurant serves better food than the restaurant across the street serve.
quests.correctedSentence: This restaurant serves better food than the restaurant across the street serves.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'the restaurant' is singular, the verb in the comparison clause should be 'serves', not the plural form 'serve'.
quests.nativeTip: The subject of this clause, 'the restaurant', is singular — does the verb match?

quests.conceptTitle: Comparison: Avoiding Redundant Objects in Than Clauses
quests.faultySentence: The new manager communicates more clearly than the old manager did it.
quests.correctedSentence: The new manager communicates more clearly than the old manager did.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Did' already substitutes for the verb and its object from the first part of the sentence, so adding 'it' is redundant; the sentence needs just 'did'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Did' already stands in for the earlier action — does the sentence need 'it' as well?

quests.conceptTitle: Comparison: Than, Not That
quests.faultySentence: This job requires more experience that the last one did.
quests.correctedSentence: This job requires more experience than the last one did.
quests.ruleExplanation: Comparisons use 'than', not 'that', so the sentence needs 'more experience than the last one did'.
quests.nativeTip: Comparisons use a specific word that sounds similar to 'that' but is spelled differently — which one?

quests.conceptTitle: Comparison: Than, Not Then
quests.faultySentence: The revised proposal has less errors then the first draft.
quests.correctedSentence: The revised proposal has less errors than the first draft.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Than' is used for comparisons, while 'then' refers to time sequence; the sentence needs 'less errors than the first draft'.
quests.nativeTip: One of these words shows sequence in time, and the other is used for comparisons — which one fits here?

quests.conceptTitle: Comparison: Than, Not Then
quests.faultySentence: Since the renovation, the store attracts more customers then it did last year.
quests.correctedSentence: Since the renovation, the store attracts more customers than it did last year.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since this is a comparison, not a time sequence, the sentence needs 'than', not 'then': 'more customers than it did last year'.
quests.nativeTip: Is this word showing a sequence in time or making a comparison?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Matching Gerunds in a List
quests.faultySentence: The manager's responsibilities include scheduling shifts, resolving conflicts, and to train new hires.
quests.correctedSentence: The manager's responsibilities include scheduling shifts, resolving conflicts, and training new hires.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'scheduling' and 'resolving' are gerunds, the last item should also be a gerund: 'training', not the infinitive 'to train'.
quests.nativeTip: The other responsibilities are in the -ing form — should the last one match?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Matching Word Forms in a List
quests.faultySentence: The report was clear, concise, and it persuaded the readers.
quests.correctedSentence: The report was clear, concise, and persuasive.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'clear' and 'concise' are adjectives, the third item should match that form: 'persuasive', not the full clause 'it persuaded the readers'.
quests.nativeTip: The first two items are adjectives — should the third item also be an adjective?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Matching Word Forms in a List
quests.faultySentence: Candidates should have strong communication skills, relevant experience, and be able to work in teams.
quests.incorrectPart: and be able to work in teams
quests.correctedSentence: Candidates should have strong communication skills, relevant experience, and the ability to work in teams.
quests.correctedPart: and the ability to work in teams
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'skills' and 'experience' are nouns, the last item should also be a noun phrase: 'the ability to work in teams', not the verb phrase 'be able to work in teams'.
quests.nativeTip: The other items in this list are nouns — should the last item also be a noun?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Matching Gerunds in a List
quests.faultySentence: The course teaches budgeting, saving strategies, and how you should invest wisely.
quests.incorrectPart: and how you should invest wisely
quests.correctedSentence: The course teaches budgeting, saving strategies, and investing wisely.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'budgeting' and 'saving' are gerunds, the last item should also be a gerund: 'investing', not the clause 'how you should invest'.
quests.nativeTip: The other items in this list are gerunds — should the last one match?

quests.conceptTitle: Comparison: Avoiding Redundant Repetition
quests.faultySentence: The new engine is more efficient than the previous engine was efficient.
quests.incorrectPart: than the previous engine was efficient
quests.correctedSentence: The new engine is more efficient than the previous one was.
quests.ruleExplanation: Repeating 'efficient' at the end is redundant since it's already stated once; the sentence needs 'than the previous one was'.
quests.nativeTip: Does the comparison need to repeat the adjective 'efficient' a second time?

quests.conceptTitle: Parallelism: Matching Word Forms in a List
quests.faultySentence: A great leader should be decisive, empathetic, and communicating clearly with the team.
quests.incorrectPart: and communicating clearly with the team
quests.correctedSentence: A great leader should be decisive, empathetic, and communicative.
quests.ruleExplanation: Since 'decisive' and 'empathetic' are adjectives, the last item should match: 'communicative', not the verb phrase 'communicating clearly with the team'.
quests.nativeTip: The other qualities are adjectives following 'should be' — should the last one also be an adjective?
